name: Bear Put Spread (Long Put Vertical)
summary: Buy a higher-strike put, sell a lower-strike put in the same expiry; a defined-risk debit bet on a decline, cheaper than an outright put.

legs.strike_rule: Long put at 0.45-0.60 delta (ATM-to-slightly-ITM) for directional conviction, or 0.35 delta for a cheaper lottery-style structure.
Short put = long strike - width; short leg 0.15-0.30 delta. Width sized so debit <= 50% of width.

max_profit: (width * 100) - net debit, if the underlying is below the short strike at expiry
breakevens: long put strike - net debit per share

greeks.delta: negative, roughly -0.20 to -0.35 per 1-lot at entry
greeks.gamma: positive while OTM, turns negative past the short strike
greeks.theta: negative while OTM (-$0.5 to -$3/day per 1-lot), positive once ITM
greeks.vega: positive when the spread is OTM -- note equity put skew means you buy the expensive put and sell the cheaper one, so this structure is systematically more expensive than the call mirror

typical_dte: 30-45 DTE swing, 7-21 DTE for event-driven, 0DTE for intraday downside momentum
when_to_use: IV rank <= 40 with a bearish trigger: price below a declining 20-EMA, a break of a 20-day low, or a failed rally into resistance. Because put skew is steep, only use this when you genuinely want defined-risk downside; otherwise a bear call spread collects better premium for the same view.
entry_rules: IV rank <= 40 (you are buying premium, and skew already taxes you).
Directional gate: last close < 20-EMA AND 20-EMA < 50-SMA, or a break below the prior 20-day low on >1.5x average volume.
Long put delta 0.35-0.60; short put delta 0.15-0.30.
Both legs OI >= 500, bid/ask <= 10% of mid.
Submit as one MLeg limit order at the mid; reprice in $0.01 steps up to mid + 25% of the quoted spread, then cancel.
management_rules: Take profit at 65% of max profit.
Stop: close at 50% loss of the debit, or if the underlying closes back above the 20-EMA.
Time stop: close at 10 DTE if the spread mid is below the entry debit.
Roll down only after a > 1.5 ATR favorable move and only by closing the existing spread at >= 50% profit first.
Never average down on a losing long vertical.
exit_rules: Hard rule: flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: if the short put is ITM by any amount at 15:30 ET on expiration day, close the whole spread at once.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: any day the short put is ITM with extrinsic < $0.10, close that session -- deep ITM short puts get exercised early for the carry.
If both strikes are deep ITM at 5 DTE (underlying < short strike - 2%), close for near-max profit; the last few cents are not worth assignment exposure.
assignment_risk: Only the short put can be assigned, which would deliver 100 long shares per contract at the short strike. The long put covers the economics but the system must never accept the shares. Early exercise is driven by interest carry on deep ITM puts, not dividends.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 per leg, bid/ask <= 10% of mid; downside strikes in a selloff can widen sharply -- use limit orders exclusively.
common_mistakes: Buying put debit spreads at elevated IV rank (double-paying through skew and vol); paying more than half the width; holding through a bounce hoping for a retest; letting the short leg sit ITM into expiry.
zero_dte_notes: Usable for intraday downside momentum on SPY/QQQ. 0.45/0.25 delta strikes computed locally, entry 09:45-13:30 ET, 50% profit target, -60% stop, hard flatten 15:30 ET. Downside 0DTE moves are faster than upside ones -- expect better payoff but worse fills.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
